evidence:
Source-based row-28 audit found no concrete duplicated scored outcome, subsumption or incompatible product demand among 74 functional, 6 polish and 6 visual criteria plus the two zero-mass gates. Workbook Quality Checks A29:D29 forbids duplicate/subsuming/incompatible criteria; Internal Quality Checks E29 permits a shared flow, and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md requires independent credit for separately useful promises. I applied those together rather than treating shared setup as either automatic duplication or blanket permission to bundle outcomes.

All task-relative paths below resolve beneath .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-10-01-extension-scope2/task/. Functional prompt.md lines 9-11 and 98-113 explicitly give each evidence key one scored owner, distinguish shared successful control facts from sibling verdicts, and preserve valid partial observations. The concrete separations hold: tests/scored/functional/judge.toml lines 73-84 and 493-497 distinguish completed Stop suppression, actual visible retention, and subsequent execution; prompt.md lines 159-161 provide independent successful-render and handler controls. Lines 381-392 and 528-532 of judge.toml distinguish stale-server refusal, dirty-editor retention/feedback, and deliberate reapplication; prompt.md lines 438-443 preserves recorded draft fields for later reapplication even if retention failed. Restart readback, example inventory and later write have different observations and an independent write fallback (judge.toml lines 360-378; prompt.md lines 426-432). Error message, source line, rollback and recovery are separate results (for example judge.toml lines 178-196 and 451-455; prompt.md lines 279-286). Auto-run suppression uses successful automatic and manual executions as controls, not a second score for the debounce outcome; manual Run additionally proves the on-state without a queued edit (prompt.md lines 394-400).

Polish names, keyboard reachability, visible focus, and successful library navigation have different bars, including preserved focus credit for reached controls when another is unreachable (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml lines 26-59). Workspace organisation concerns recognising and locating surfaces (line 68), not executing the functional operations. Visual prompt.md lines 13-31 separates feature behavior from craft, assigns mobile operability/clipping to Polish, assigns font choices versus desktop geometry to different visual owners, and prohibits reusing the same observation to lower hierarchy, overall craft or responsive consistency. Visual judge.toml lines 24, 54 and 99 repeat those ownership boundaries. Gate controls prove minimum execution/server backing and carry no reward mass (tests/scoring.toml lines 1-3), rather than awarding repeated credit for detailed scored promises.

Counterexample analysis: a partial app which suppresses completed handlers by deleting the preview should retain Stop-suppression credit but fail preview preservation; a stale-write-refusing server which discards the dirty editor should pass server refusal, fail draft preservation, and may still pass manual reapplication from the recorded draft. A dead Auto-run feature cannot gain off-state suppression credit because actual automatic execution is required. These examples do not expose an independence bypass. A conforming alternative that retains static successful pictures, uses native focus/composite controls, or presents mobile tabs remains permitted, so I found no conflicting product demands from those alternatives. A simple native visual presentation is explicitly eligible for full credit. No new mutation or configured judge run was performed, so these are criterion-application counterexamples, not measured model scores.
